description:
crates/outram-mc-libs/src/geometry/lattice/mod.rs, HexLattice::distance.

The port reconstructed ALL THREE components of the lattice-frame position from
the tile offset (r_local + center_offset). The axial branch at the end of the
function then compares that z against +/- 0.5*pitch[1], which is a TILE-LOCAL
half-height. The comparison is therefore wrong by the tile's own z offset, and
returns a NEGATIVE distance-to-boundary for every tile except the one sitting
at offset zero.

OpenMC builds a hybrid position at the CALL site instead (src/geometry.cpp:459-467):
x,y in the lattice frame, z tile-local. Upstream also guards the result --
'if (d_lat < 0) p.mark_as_lost(...)' -- which this port does not.

WHY IT SURVIVED: the error cancels exactly when the tile z-offset is zero, i.e.
n_axial == 1, and from_rings_3d had unit tests only (no integration test, no
example). Measured on the HTR-10 core model 2026-09-17: n_axial=1 -> 0 negatives;
n_axial=2 -> 8.2e6; n_axial=20 -> 1.7e7 (worst -7.7e3 cm).

IMPACT: the neutron steps BACKWARDS and oscillates until MAX_EVENTS kills it.
On the HTR-10 core this ended 68-88 % of all histories, and because a stuck
history is scored as a leak it was INVISIBLE in k -- the model reported k=0
with no error. After the fix: k_eff = 0.707506 +/- 0.006010, 0 lost, 0 stuck,
0 negative, 499 collisions/history.

FIXED in the same change. Needs a regression test: a 3-D hex lattice with
n_axial > 1 must never return a negative tile distance.
title: HexLattice::distance used a lattice-frame z against a tile-local bound (3-D hex only)

description: op-cjw.17 landed the covard numeric transform, expndo pair enumeration, corr rsd sourcing, and BOXER press/setfor writer — but covard reads a CONSTRUCTED in-memory matrix because ERRORR's covariance-output kernels (covout/colaps) are unported, so no real ERRORR covariance tape/byte-stream exists to decode. Needed: ERRORR covout/colaps writers, then the covard tape reader (covr.f90:740-886) + expndo tape scan (:526-556), plus byte-exact 1P float formatting in press_text. Human-verify: auto-vs-cross rsd sourcing against a real ERRORR tape.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: 2026-09-10 wave 4: DONE. covard tape half (covr.f90:740-886) + expndo scan (:526-556) ported in src/covr/tape.rs over the crate Tape reader; byte-exact BOXER text in boxer_text.rs; parse_boxer_text reader added for V&V. Human-verify point (auto vs cross rsd sourcing) is now oracle-verified: cross-pair correlation records (matype=4, e.g. 128/1 x 128/16, 9237/18 x 9237/102) are byte-identical to NJOY. FINDING (measured, fixed): crate ERRORR covout zeroed every output element with |v|<=1e-20 (covout.rs:454); upstream errorr.f90:7563-7568 uses eps only to bracket ig2lo/ng2 and writes interior sub-eps elements verbatim (NJOY U-238 tape carries e-49..e-69 values). Effect: U-238 tier-2 BOXER agreed on 805/3818 lines (press encodes each tiny value as a distinct run). Removing the zeroing -> 3818/3818 and 3385/3385 identical; errorr_mf33_golden still passes (1e-12 floor had hidden it). NEGATIVE RESULT: none needed - hypothesis predicted more identical lines and got all of them.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: 2026-09-10 wave 4: DONE and pushed (develop 582beece + 3062ad78). covard tape half + expndo scan (src/covr/tape.rs), library driver (library.rs), byte-exact BOXER text (boxer_text.rs). tests/covr_boxer_golden.rs: 18/18 tier-1 byte-identical vs NJOY2016 covr; 18/18 tier-2 (crate ERRORR tape) byte-identical after the covout sub-eps fix. Full suite 741 passed / 0 failed / 8 ignored (34 binaries).

title: COVR: real ERRORR covariance tape I/O (covout/colaps + covard/expndo tape scan) (op-cjw.17 gap)

description:
s31. Synchronisation belongs ENTIRELY to Kovan, not to kopitiam-pdf or kopitiam-neovim. PaperSession owns kopitiam-pdf reader + ResearchRecord index + kopitiam-neovim editor, with a SyncController between them.

Three policies: FOLLOW (soft contextual sync -- when PDF page 87 is visible, find artifacts anchored there and softly follow/highlight); EDIT (never yank the editor viewport while the user is actively typing); EXPLICIT JUMP (clicking go-to-source synchronises immediately). s46's 'Bidirectional navigation' acceptance scenario: artifact -> exact PDF page/region, and PDF context -> relevant artifacts.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Implemented: src/sync.rs (SyncController). Deliberately PDF-reader-agnostic -- speaks only in page numbers (u32) and Artifact references, never a PdfReaderState/kopitiam_pdf type, so it can wire to EITHER the legacy digitiser/gui/desktop/pdf_reader.rs (usable today) or the eventual reusable kopitiam-pdf reader with no change to this module. Three policies as three methods, not a selectable enum (s31 describes three interaction kinds, not one setting): follow_page() self-gates on allow_follow() (never forgotten at a call site); jump_to_source() reads SourceAnchor::first_page()+region for artifact->PDF; artifact_at_editor_line() is the PDF->editor/editor->PDF counterpart (which artifact currently encloses the cursor). SCOPE NOTE, stated in the module doc: live GUI wiring of a real reader+editor pair through this controller is deferred -- PaperSession does not yet own either side (op-9vo6.11 is still blocked on the kopitiam-pdf 0.3.2+ publish), and this bead's own dependency graph already reflected that (op-9vo6.18 -> op-9vo6.11). What ships here is the tested synchronisation logic, ready to wire once that lands. 5 tests.

title: kovan redesign 18: PDF <-> Markdown synchronization (SyncController)

description: The tampines crate's examples/fhr_sim_v2 is a byte-identical copy of the engine example but the tampines crate does NOT depend on outram-park-digital-twin-engine, so it cannot reuse app_scaffold::{ThreadHealth, spawn_monitored, show_crash_modal_if_crashed} as-is. Options: (a) add outram-park-digital-twin-engine as a dev-dependency of tampines (closes a normal->dev dependency cycle since engine depends on tampines; cargo permits one dev edge but verify), then mirror the 2-file edit; or (b) inline a small self-contained copy of ThreadHealth+modal in the tampines example. Engine-side feature done in op-4wv (crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine: app_scaffold/crash.rs + wired fhr_sim_v2 + htgr_sim_v1).
title: tampines fhr_sim_v2 copy: mirror thread-crash restart modal (needs engine dep decision)

description: Idea (logged 2026-07-22, outside working hours — not started). Give outram-mc-libs a ratatui TUI to pick a preconfigured geometry (e.g. Godiva/Jezebel bare sphere, pincell, TRISO/pebble stochastic-media cell) and a small set of preset materials, then launch a transport run (k-eff / absorption) and show live convergence. A human front-end over the existing pebble_beds/geometry/material + stochastic (CLS/SCLS) paths. Precedent: kovan-tui. Android/Termux rule applies (TUI in-scope; target-gate desktop-only bits). Design + scope TBD in an active window.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: REQUIREMENTS (2026-07-22): MOBILE-FIRST ratatui TUI, interactable via TOUCHSCREEN. Features: (1) preconfigured COMMON GEOMETRIES to pick from: pebble bed, LWR cell, TMSR-like pebble bed, bare-metal sphere (Godiva/Jezebel); (2) settings selectable in the TUI: GPU vs CPU, number of batches, (histories/gen, active/inactive gens, etc.); (3) show the NEUTRON SPECTRUM in the TUI, OVERLAID with the relevant cross sections (shared log-energy axis). Companion to the njoy XS-browser TUI (op-et4) — the spectrum overlay pulls from the same XS visualization. Android/Termux rule applies.

title: outram-mc: TUI for preconfigured geometries + materials
